claim_ceiling: Empirical-Bayes random-intercept reference baseline for related environments with one scalar context covariate; not a full hierarchical Bayesian retrieval and not a life detector.

literature_comparator.citation: Constantinou, Shorttle, Cranmer & Rimmer (2026), Comparative biosignatures with systemic retrievals, MNRAS 547, stag316
literature_comparator.reported_method: Hierarchical Bayesian model of system-linked abiotic trends, Bayesian leave-one-out prediction and comparative biosignature anomalies; poor fit under both abiotic and biotic models remains unknown unknown.
literature_comparator.this_implementation: Small empirical-Bayes method-of-moments random-intercept reference only. Does not claim parity with the paper's HBM or evolutionary retrieval.

model.system_effect: normal random-intercept empirical-Bayes partial pooling, with method-of-moments between-system variance
model.fit_population: only observations explicitly tagged qualified_abiotic_control and carrying a qualification evidence reference
model.target_evaluation: leave-target-out by construction; candidate/unresolved observations never enter the fit
model.predictive_variance: within-system residual + posterior system-intercept variance + candidate measurement variance + approximate common-slope variance
model.unsupported_context_rule: reject extrapolation outside the qualified-control context range for that system
model.threshold: caller-declared standardized residual threshold; no universal biological threshold

alternative_model_comparison.input: separately supplied predicted_mean and predictive_stddev, with a model_id
alternative_model_comparison.score: Gaussian log predictive density on the held-out observation, including candidate measurement uncertainty
alternative_model_comparison.rule: A model is adequate only when its absolute standardized residual is within the caller-declared threshold. If both are inadequate, preserve UnknownUnknown. A preference requires the adequate model and minimum log-score advantage.

cases.purpose: Show how a pooled baseline can falsely flag a target because related systems have different abiotic offsets.

expected.interpretation: The candidate follows its own system's abiotic trend despite differing strongly from a global pooled line.

cases.purpose: Detect a target that departs from its own system baseline while remaining inside the qualified context range.

expected.interpretation: Model-relative outlier only; not evidence of life or biogenicity.

cases.purpose: Ensure high-valued but unqualified observations do not contaminate the abiotic baseline.
Avoid converting out-of-support model extrapolation into a confident anomaly.
Require a qualified local baseline before evaluating a new system.
Ensure the system-level prior center is not dominated by systems with more sampled worlds.
Demonstrate an independently supplied alternative model that predicts a comparative anomaly better than the abiotic baseline.

expected.claim_ceiling: relative predictive result only; not proof of life or biogenicity

cases.purpose: Preserve an out-of-family observation when neither the qualified abiotic baseline nor the alternative mechanism model explains it.
Prevent a forced choice when both abiotic and alternative models adequately predict the same observation.
Ensure a poor alternative model does not create a biosignature claim when the abiotic baseline explains the candidate.

anti_leakage: Only QualifiedAbioticControl observations are used in fitting.
Every qualified control requires an explicit qualification evidence reference.
Each qualified control must have a unique independence_group.
Candidate and Unresolved observations are excluded even when present in the fit input slice.
Target observations are evaluated against a model fitted without the target.
Time frames and repeated measurements from the same physical world are not independent worlds.
Context outside the qualified control range is rejected rather than extrapolated.
Alternative-model predictions must be produced and versioned independently; the baseline evaluator cannot author or validate its own alternative model.
If both models fail the declared predictive-adequacy threshold, preserve the candidate as UnknownUnknownBothModelsInadequate.
limitations: Empirical-Bayes moment estimates, not full HBM posterior inference.
No explicit biotic evolutionary model is included; the output is an anomaly score/disposition only.
System-specific stochastic processes not represented by the covariate may produce anomalies.
Qualification errors in the abiotic controls can bias the baseline.
